title: watch
summary: Install or remove a shell hook that records each command with its folder.
notes: `watch start` adds a block to your profile. The block calls `cwm watch log` after every command. There is no background process.
Commands that look like they hold secrets (password, token, secret, api key, Authorization, bearer, private key) are never stored.
Commands that start with a space are never stored.
`-ex` takes a comma separated list of command names to skip, for example `cwm,clear`. Run `watch start -ex ...` again to update the list.
Read the log back with `cwm get -a`. Remove duplicates with `cwm tidy watch`.
`cwm watch log` is internal. The shell hook uses it.

flags.name: -ex, --exclude <list>
flags.desc: Command names to skip, comma separated.

subcommands.name: start
subcommands.desc: Install the hook in your shell profile.

subcommands.name: status
subcommands.desc: Show whether the hook is active and the exclusion list.

examples.title: Start recording, skipping cwm and clear
examples.output:
Watch session started successfully!
  Profile updated:   C:\Users\you\.bashrc
  Excluded Commands: cwm,clear
  Not recorded:      commands that look like they contain secrets, and commands that start with a space
  Activate it now with: source ~/.bashrc
